title: Tenant-aware semantic-split scheduler for init+generate pipeline
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem:
Current init+generate (prefill+decode) pipeline uses static split thresholds that do not account for per-tenant request characteristics (prompt length distribution, attention locality, cost tier). That causes either: (a) over-splitting for tenants with dense attention patterns and long KV lifetimes (worse throughput), or (b) under-splitting for bursty low-latency tenants (long tail latency spikes).

Goal:
Design and ship a tenant-aware \"semantic-split\" scheduling policy that: (1) dynamically chooses split points based on per-request attention/semantic signals and tenant SLOs, (2) steers kernel selection hints to the runtime (dense vs sparse attention kernels, small-seq optimized kernels), and (3) enforces a fairness decayer so high-volume tenants cannot starve latency-sensitive ones. Target runtime-1.28 as the first opt-in experiment.

High-level approach:
- Signal extraction: lightweight attention-locality estimator runs in prefill stage to compute an \"attention density\" score and a semantic-boundary heuristic (based on cue tokens and sentence breaks).
- Split policy: use a three-tier decision: NO_SPLIT | SEMANTIC_SPLIT (at sentence/cue boundaries) | MICRO_SPLIT (time/phase-based small slices). Decision factors: attention density, tenant latency SLO, recent p95, and queue backlog.
- Kernel hinting: attach kernel hints (dense/sparse, kv-cache-friendly) to microbatches so the kernel selector can probe preferred kernels before final scheduling.
- Fairness decayer: a per-tenant credit bucket that decays a tenant's scheduling weight if their p95 > target for N intervals; credits slowly replenish when under SLO. This avoids immediate demotion oscillation via hysteresis.
- Hysteresis and stability: require decision changes only after 2 consecutive windows to avoid flapping; minimum split duration of 250ms.
- Fallbacks: if a fastpath kernel fails to initialize or a tenant experiences degradation, fall back to conservative full-slice execution and trigger an automated roll-forward metric.

Metrics and success criteria:
- Latency: reduce p95 for latency-sensitive tenants by >= 20% in opt-in cohorts.
- Throughput: overall token/sec for mixed workloads should not drop by more than 5% for default pools.
- Cost: no more than 3% increase in GPU cycles for opt-in tenants versus baseline.
- Fairness: tenant SLO violations must decrease for high-priority tenants while high-volume tenants see bounded degradation.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Complexity vs signal value: attention-density estimator must be sub-1ms; initially use sampled attention statistics during prefill rather than full attention matrix analysis.
- Kernel hinting overhead: hints add metadata to microbatches; we limit hint size to <64 bytes and aggregate hints per batch to avoid serialization overhead.
- Per-tenant state memory: credit buckets use 8 bytes per tenant in the scheduler; acceptable for current tenant counts but will need sharding beyond 100k tenants.

Experiment plan:
1) Simulation: extend existing scheduler sim harness with semantic-split knobs and run mixed tenant traces (internal corpora + synthetic burst traces).
2) Canary: opt-in Canary group (10% of production traffic on a dedicated pool) for 2 weeks. Metrics tracked via dashboard runtime/scheduler/semantic_split/* and rollback thresholds defined.
3) Rollout: staged 25%/50%/100% with automated rollback if cluster-level p95 increases >10% or error rates spike.

Implementation tasks (high level):
- Scheduler core: implement semantic-split decision module + credit-bucket logic (ENG task A).
- Runtime contract: wire kernel hint metadata to scheduler -> runtime kernel selector (ENG task B).
- Lightweight estimator: implement prefill attention-density sampler in prefill path (ENG task C).
- Telemetry: dashboards, histograms, and tracing hooks for split decisions, kernel hints, and tenant credit state (ENG task D).
- Tests: unit tests for split decision logic, sim harness scenario, integration tests for hint propagation (ENG task E).

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (internal Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/semantic-split-scheduler
- Simulation harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler-sim/pull/189
- Prototype runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345
- Dashboard (grafana): https://dash.redwood.ai/d/runtime/semantic-split-overview

Risks and mitigation:
- Incorrect attention heuristics: keep estimator conservative, start with coarse bins and iterate with labeled telemetry.
- Memory blowup for credits: implement LRU sharding and eviction for cold tenants.
updates: 2026-03-02: Initial design sketch posted to Confluence and synced with product. Review requested from reliability and kernel teams.
2026-03-05: Prototype estimator implemented; microbench shows 0.6ms median overhead for sampled attention stats on A100. Posting PR #2345.

2026-03-08: Simulation results (mixed workload v1) indicate 22% p95 reduction for latency cohort with 2.8% throughput loss on heavy batches. Added fairness decayer to address starvation observed in sims.

2026-03-11: Design review with Kernel team: recommended reducing hint size and exposing 'probed_kernel' feedback to scheduler to learn kernel success rates. Action: add feedback loop in scheduler (task B.2).
2026-03-14: Canary config templated and canary pool provisioned. QA smoke tests passed; monitoring widgets added. Starting canary rollout tomorrow.
2026-03-14: Blockers: need final sign-off from Security on metadata exposure (ticketed to SEC-402). If sign-off delayed, we will mask tenant IDs in hints and use hashed tenant keys.
acceptance_criteria: Opt-in canary demonstrates p95 reduction >= 20% for latency-sensitive tenants without >10% overall cluster latency regression.
Kernel hints are consumed by runtime: we have probe feedback and a histogram of kernel selection success rates.
Telemetry surfaces per-tenant credit state and split decision reasons for at least 30 days retention in staging.
All new code has unit tests and integration tests; PRs linked in ticket; documentation updated on Confluence.
